PRO FORMA 
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION AGREEMENT 
This LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”) is made and 
entered into as of [Date] (the “Execution Date”) by and between [LEGAL NAME OF 
TRANSMISSION OWNER], a [New York corporation / municipal instrumentality / public 
benefit corporation] organized and existing under the laws of the State of New York, with offices 
at [Address] (“Transmission Owner” or “TO”), and [LEGAL NAME OF CUSTOMER], a [entity 
type and jurisdiction], with offices at [Address] (“Customer”). Transmission Owner and 
Customer are each referred to herein as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” 
RECITALS 
WHEREAS, Transmission Owner owns and operates, among other things, electric transmission 
facilities that form part of the New York State Transmission System, provides transmission 
service over such facilities through the New York Independent System Operator, Inc. (“NYISO”) 
pursuant to the Tariff on file with FERC, and [provides electric delivery service pursuant to its 
retail tariff on file with the NYPSC]; 
WHEREAS, Customer intends to design, construct, own, operate, and maintain a large load 
facility, together with the associated Customer Attachment Facilities, located at [Site Address] 
(the “Load Facility”), as more particularly described in Exhibit A; 
WHEREAS, Customer has requested that the Load Facility be interconnected to Transmission 
Owner’s transmission system at the Point of Interconnection identified in Exhibit B, with a 
Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand of [●] MW; 
WHEREAS, Transmission Owner, alone or in coordination with NYISO, has conducted or will 
conduct a System Impact Study, a Facilities Study, and such other engineering, detailed design, 
and special studies as are required by Applicable Laws and Regulations, Applicable Reliability 
Standards, and Good Utility Practice to determine the effect of the Load Facility on the TO 
System and the New York State Transmission System and the need, if any, for TO Attachment 
Facilities and the Customer Attachment Facilities and Network Upgrades[, and the Parties have 
entered into or will enter into a Cost Recovery Agreement dated [●] with respect to the Network 
Upgrades and TO Attachment Facilities determined to be necessary as a result of such studies]; 
WHEREAS, Transmission Owner will design, construct, own, operate, and maintain the TO 
Attachment Facilities and, if applicable, the Network Upgrades, and Customer will design, 
construct, own, operate, and maintain the Customer Attachment Facilities, in each case at 
Customer’s cost to the extent provided in this Agreement or the Cost Recovery Agreement; and 
WHEREAS, the Parties wish to set forth the terms and conditions under which the Load Facility 
will be interconnected with, and operated in parallel with, the transmission system. 
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth 
herein, and intending to be legally bound, the Parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE 1 
DEFINITIONS 
Whenever used in this Agreement with initial capitalization, the following terms have the 
meanings specified in this Article 1. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Agreement 
have the meanings given in the Tariff or the NYISO Services Tariff, as applicable. 
1.1 
“Affiliate” means, with respect to a person or entity, any other person or entity 
directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with such 
person or entity. “Control” means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the 
power to direct the management or policies of a person or entity; a voting interest 
of ten percent (10%) or more creates a rebuttable presumption of control. 
1.2 
“Applicable Laws and Regulations” means all duly promulgated or issued 
applicable federal, state, and local laws, treaties, statutes, regulations, rules, 
ordinances, codes, decrees, judgments, permits, licenses, approvals, directives, and 
judicial, executive, or administrative orders of any Governmental Authority, 
including Environmental Law and the NYISO tariffs, manuals, and technical 
bulletins, in each case as amended from time to time. 
1.3 
“Applicable Reliability Standards” means the requirements and guidelines of 
NERC, NPCC, and NYSRC, and of the transmission district to which the Load 
Facility is directly interconnected, as amended from time to time; provided that no 
Party waives its right to challenge the applicability or validity of any such 
requirement or guideline as applied to it. 
1.4 
“Attachment Facilities” means all facilities and equipment between the Load 
Facility and the Point of Interconnection, including any modifications, additions, 
or upgrades that are necessary to physically and electrically interconnect the Load 
Facility to the New York State Transmission System. Attachment Facilities are sole 
use facilities and shall not include Network Upgrades. Attachment Facilities may 
include equipment (e.g., metering) necessary for the entity authorized to serve load 
within a Transmission District, if Transmission Owner is not the entity authorized 
to serve that load. 
1.5 
“Breach” means the failure of a Party to perform any material term, condition, or 
obligation of this Agreement, and “Breaching Party” means the Party that has 
committed a Breach. 
1.6 
“Business Day” means Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays and 
[TO holidays].  
1.7 
“Calendar Day” means any day, including Saturday, Sunday, or a federal holiday. 
1.8 
“Commercial Operation” means the status of the Load Facility once (a) the Load 
Facility has successfully completed testing and commissioning in accordance with 
this Agreement and the Operating Documents; (b) the In-Service Date has occurred 
for the TO Attachment Facilities and Network Upgrades, and the Customer 
Attachment Facilities have been completed, energized, and placed into service, in 
each case to the extent necessary for the Load Facility to take firm electric service 
at or above its designated minimum capacity commitment; (c) all conditions

precedent to Delivery Service have been satisfied; (d) Transmission Owner has 
issued Permission to Operate; and (e) the Load Facility is in operation. 
1.9 
“Commercial Operation Date” means the date on which the Load Facility has 
achieved energization and begins taking firm electric service at or above its 
designated minimum capacity commitment, as confirmed by notice substantially in 
the form of Exhibit H. 
1.10 
“Cost Recovery Agreement” means the [Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement] 
between Transmission Owner and Customer dated [●], attached as or referenced in 
Exhibit G, which governs Customer’s responsibility for and payment of the costs 
of the Network Upgrades and the TO Attachment Facilities, including through the 
Large Load Upgrade Charge (as defined therein), as amended from time to time. 
1.11 
“Customer Attachment Facilities” means all facilities and equipment on 
Customer’s side of the Point of Change of Ownership that are owned or controlled 
by Customer, including but not limited to breakers, switches, transformers, bus 
work, cables, relays, System Protection Facilities, communication and telemetry 
equipment, and associated civil and structural works, as described and shown in 
Exhibits A and C. 
1.12 
“Default” means the failure of a Breaching Party to cure a Breach in accordance 
with Article 16. 
1.13 
“Delivery Service” means the electric delivery service provided to Customer 
pursuant to the applicable Tariff, for delivery of energy from the New York State 
Transmission System to the Load Facility. 
1.14 
“Emergency State” means a condition or situation that, in the reasonable judgment 
of a Party or NYISO, (a) presents an imminent threat to the safety of persons or 
property, or (b) requires automatic or immediate manual action to prevent or limit 
loss of, or threatens the integrity, reliability, or security of, the TO System or the 
New York State Transmission System. 
1.15 
“Environmental Law” means Applicable Laws and Regulations relating to 
pollution or protection of the environment or natural resources. 
1.16 
“Exceedance Event” means the Load Facility exceeding the energy or demand 
stated for the applicable period as further defined in Article 3.7 and Exhibits A and 
C.  
1.17 
“FERC” means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or any successor 
agency. 
1.18 
“Force Majeure” has the meaning set forth in Article 16.1. 
1.19 
“Good Utility Practice” means any of the practices, methods, and acts engaged in 
or approved by a significant portion of the electric utility industry during the 
relevant time period, or any of the practices, methods, and acts which, in the 
exercise of reasonable judgment in light of the facts known at the time the decision 
was made, could have been expected to accomplish the desired result at a 
reasonable cost consistent with good business practices, reliability, safety, and 
expedition. Good Utility Practice is not intended to be limited to the optimum

practice, method, or act to the exclusion of all others, but rather to delineate 
acceptable practices, methods, or acts generally accepted in the region. 
1.20 
“Governmental Authority” means any federal, state, local, or other 
governmental, regulatory, or administrative agency, court, commission, 
department, board, legislature, tribunal, or other governmental authority having 
jurisdiction over a Party, its facilities, or the services it provides. 
1.21 
“Hazardous Substances” means any chemical, material, or substance defined as 
or included in the definition of “hazardous substances,” “hazardous wastes,” 
“hazardous materials,” “toxic substances,” “pollutants,” “contaminants,” or words 
of similar meaning and regulatory effect under any Environmental Law. 
1.22 
“In-Service Date” means the date on which the TO Attachment Facilities and 
Network Upgrades are energized, as set forth in Exhibit D. 
1.23 
“Load Ramp Projection” has the meaning set forth in Article 3.5. 
1.24 
“Material Modification” means any modification to the Load Facility or 
Customer Attachment Facilities that, in Transmission Owner’s reasonable 
judgment, may require changes to the TO Attachment Facilities and the Customer 
Attachment Facilities or Network Upgrades or may otherwise materially affect 
system reliability, including (a) an increase or decrease in maximum demand 
beyond levels specified in the Operating Documents; (b) a material change in power 
factor, ramp rate, or other operating characteristics, including those reported in the 
NYISO Load Interconnection Data Request; (c) relocation of the Point of 
Interconnection; or (d) any modification having a material impact on the cost or 
timing of any interconnection request with a later queue position. 
1.25 
“Maximum Annual Energy” means the maximum annual energy (in MWh) to be 
consumed by the Load Facility, as measured at the Point of Interconnection during 
any calendar year, as set forth in Exhibit A, prorated for any partial calendar year. 
1.26 
“Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand” means the maximum peak demand for 
Firm Withdrawal Service of the Load Facility at any time, as set forth in Exhibit A, 
not to exceed the amount studied in the System Impact Study and Facilities Study.  
1.27 
“Metering Equipment” means all revenue-quality metering equipment installed 
or to be installed at or near the Point of Interconnection, including instrument 
transformers, meters, data acquisition equipment, transducers, remote terminal 
units, and communications equipment, as specified in Exhibit B. 
1.28 
“Minimum Committed Load” means [eighty percent (80%)] of the Maximum 
Load Facility Peak Demand.  
1.29 
“NERC” means the North American Electric Reliability Corporation, or its 
successor. 
1.30 
“Network Upgrades” means additions, modifications, enhancements, or 
replacements to the TO System or the New York State Transmission System at or 
beyond the Point of Interconnection, other than TO Attachment Facilities, that are 
required to accommodate the interconnection of the Load Facility and maintain 
system reliability, as identified in the System Impact Study, the Facilities Study,

and such other engineering, detailed design, and special studies, and set forth in 
Exhibit B. 
1.31 
“New York State Transmission System” means the entire New York State 
electric transmission system, including the transmission facilities under NYISO 
operational control, the transmission facilities requiring NYISO notification, and 
all remaining transmission facilities within the New York Control Area. 
1.32 
“NPCC” means the Northeast Power Coordinating Council, Inc., or its successor. 
1.33 
“NYISO” has the meaning set forth in the Recitals and includes any successor 
thereto. 
1.34 
“NYPSC” means the New York State Public Service Commission, or its successor. 
1.35 
“NYSRC” means the New York State Reliability Council, L.L.C., or its successor. 
1.36 
“Operating Documents” means the operating requirements developed by 
Transmission Owner and provided to Customer before initial energization, 
including those described in Exhibit E, and the Operations Manual described in 
Article 7.11, in each case as amended from time to time in accordance with this 
Agreement. 
1.37 
“Permission to Operate” or “PTO” means the written authorization issued by 
Transmission Owner permitting Customer to place the Load Facility into 
Commercial Operation and to take Delivery Service at the Point of Interconnection 
upon satisfaction of the conditions set forth in Article 4 and Exhibit F. 
1.38 
“Point of Change of Ownership” or “PCO” means the point described in Exhibit 
B and shown in Exhibit C. 
1.39 
“Point of Interconnection” or “POI” means the physical point, described in 
Exhibit B and shown in Exhibit C, at which the Attachment Facilities connect to 
the New York State Transmission System. 
1.40 
“Reasonable Efforts” means, with respect to an action required to be attempted or 
taken by a Party, efforts that are timely and consistent with Good Utility Practice 
and are substantially equivalent to those a Party would use to protect its own 
interests. 
1.41 
“Related Agreements” means, collectively, the Cost Recovery Agreement, the 
Security Agreement, and any other agreements listed in Exhibit G. 
1.42 
“Security Agreement” means the [Large Load Security Agreement] between the 
Parties dated [●], attached as or referenced in Exhibit G, which governs the posting, 
maintenance, adjustment, application, and release of the security Customer 
provides to Transmission Owner for the TO Attachment Facilities and Network 
Upgrades, as amended from time to time. 
1.43 
“Single Contingency Design” means a design of the interconnection under which 
service to the Load Facility may be interrupted upon the loss of a single element of 
the TO System, as described in Exhibit E.

1.44 
“System Impact Study” or “SIS” means the study performed by NYISO, in 
coordination with Transmission Owner, under Attachment LL of the Tariff 
(including the Assessment of Load Integration) to evaluate the impact of the Load 
Facility on the New York State Transmission System. 
1.45 
“Facilities Study” means the study performed by or on behalf of Transmission 
Owner under the facilities study agreement between the Parties to specify and 
estimate the cost of the TO Attachment Facilities and Network Upgrades, including 
any updates thereto. 
1.46 
“System Protection Facilities” means the equipment, including protection signal 
communications and direct transfer trip equipment, required to protect (a) the New 
York State Transmission System from faults or other disturbances occurring at the 
Load Facility and (b) the Load Facility from faults or other disturbances occurring 
on the New York State Transmission System. 
1.47 
“Tariff” means the NYISO Open Access Transmission Tariff, including 
Transmission Owner-specific rate schedules and attachments on file with and 
accepted by FERC, and, where applicable, Transmission Owner’s retail electric 
tariff on file with the NYPSC, each as amended from time to time. “NYISO 
Services Tariff” means the NYISO Market Administration and Control Area 
Services Tariff. 
1.48 
“TO Attachment Facilities” means all facilities and equipment owned or 
controlled by Transmission Owner between the Point of Interconnection and the 
Point of Change of Ownership that are constructed or modified for the purpose of 
interconnecting the Load Facility, including line taps, breakers, disconnect 
switches, bus work, metering instrument transformers (if owned by Transmission 
Owner), System Protection Facilities at a Transmission Owner substation, and 
associated civil and structural works, as described and shown in Exhibits B and C. 
1.49 
“TO Standards” means Transmission Owner’s design criteria, specifications, 
procedures, policies, guidelines, and requirements for customer interconnections, 
as provided to Customer and/or referenced in Exhibit B. 
1.50 
“TO System” means the electric facilities owned or controlled by Transmission 
Owner, including its transmission system and distribution system.  
ARTICLE 2 
EFFECTIVE DATE, TERM, AND 
TERMINATION 
2.1 
Effective Date. This Agreement shall become effective upon the later of (a) the 
Execution Date; (b) Customer’s execution and delivery of the Security Agreement 
and any other agreements listed in Exhibit G; and (c) if Transmission Owner 
determines that this Agreement must be filed with FERC or the NYPSC, the 
effective date established upon acceptance of such filing (the “Effective Date”). 
2.2 
Conditions to Interconnection Activities. The Parties’ obligations to undertake 
construction, testing, and other interconnection activities are conditioned upon (a)

completion of the System Impact Study, Facilities Study, and such other 
engineering, detailed design, and special studies as are required; (b) execution of 
any related construction or cost reimbursement agreements, the Cost Recovery 
Agreement, the Security Agreement, and any transmission service agreement 
required under the applicable Tariff (“TSA”), and receipt of required deposits and 
advance payments; (c) receipt of all Required Approvals; and (d) completion of the 
initial Operating Documents. If this Agreement is required to be filed with FERC 
or the NYPSC, Transmission Owner shall have no obligation to commence 
engineering, procurement, or construction before acceptance of such filing. 
2.3 
Term. This Agreement shall remain in effect for [fifteen (15)] years from the 
Effective Date [or, if longer, the term of the Cost Recovery Agreement] (the “Initial 
Term”) and shall thereafter automatically renew for successive [five (5)]-year 
periods unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal at least one 
hundred eighty (180) Calendar Days before the end of the then-current term, unless 
earlier terminated in accordance with this Agreement (the “Term”). Neither Party 
may deliver a notice of non-renewal while the Cost Recovery Agreement remains 
in effect. 
2.4 
Termination. This Agreement may be terminated as follows: 
(1) 
by mutual written agreement of the Parties; 
(2) 
by Customer for any reason upon at least one hundred eighty (180) Calendar 
Days’ prior written notice, subject to payment of the Net Present Value 
Residual Charge (as defined in the Cost Recovery Agreement), all amounts 
owed under this Agreement, the Security Agreement, the Cost Recovery 
Agreement, and any other related agreements, and confirmation that all 
amounts owed to NYISO for the Load Facility have been paid; such 
termination shall constitute an early termination under the Cost Recovery 
Agreement; 
(3) 
by Transmission Owner upon thirty (30) Calendar Days’ prior written 
notice if Customer fails to achieve Commercial Operation within twelve 
(12) months after Transmission Owner has completed the TO Attachment 
Facilities and any required Network Upgrades, or such later date as the 
Parties agree in writing, or if Customer fails to achieve any Customer 
milestone in Exhibit D by more than one hundred eighty (180) Calendar 
Days for reasons other than Force Majeure or Transmission Owner’s 
Breach; provided that such termination shall not relieve Customer of its 
obligations under Article 2.6, the Cost Recovery Agreement, or the Security 
Agreement; 
(4) 
by the non-defaulting Party upon a Default in accordance with Article 16; 
or 
(5) 
by either Party upon thirty (30) Calendar Days’ prior written notice if a 
Party is prevented by Force Majeure from materially performing its 
obligations for twelve (12) consecutive months; provided Customer’s 
termination under this clause shall not relieve Customer of its obligations

under Article 2.6, the Cost Recovery Agreement, or the Security 
Agreement. 
2.5 
Transmission Owner Rights Upon Customer Breach. Without limiting Article 
2.4, upon a Breach by Customer that remains uncured for ten (10) Business Days 
after notice, Transmission Owner may suspend work on the TO Attachment 
Facilities and Network Upgrades, suspend or reduce service to the Load Facility to 
the extent consistent with Applicable Laws and Regulations, and draw upon 
security under the Security Agreement, in each case until the Breach is cured. 
Customer shall bear all costs of suspension and remobilization, and milestone dates 
shall be extended as reasonably necessary. 
2.6 
Termination Costs. Upon any termination other than for Transmission Owner’s 
Default, Customer shall pay all costs incurred or irrevocably committed by 
Transmission Owner as of the date of termination that are Customer’s responsibility 
under this Agreement, including cancellation costs for orders and contracts for TO 
Attachment Facilities and the Customer Attachment Facilities, Network Upgrades, 
and equipment, and all costs of the removal, relocation, retirement, or other 
disposition of such facilities to the extent required by Good Utility Practice and 
necessary to restore the New York State Transmission System to a reliable 
condition in accordance with Applicable Reliability Standards, in each case except 
to the extent such costs are recovered under the Cost Recovery Agreement. Each 
Party shall use Reasonable Efforts to mitigate such costs. Early termination and 
stranded cost payments, including the Net Present Value Residual Charge (as 
defined in the Cost Recovery Agreement) for the TO Attachment Facilities and 
Network Upgrades, are further governed by the Cost Recovery Agreement and the 
Security Agreement.  
2.7 
Disconnection Upon Termination. Upon termination, Transmission Owner shall 
take all appropriate steps to disconnect the Load Facility from the New York State 
Transmission System consistent with Good Utility Practice, and Customer shall 
cooperate with any disconnection and bear all costs of disconnection. 
2.8 
Survival. This Agreement shall continue in effect after termination to the extent 
necessary to provide for final billings and payments; to permit the determination 
and enforcement of liability and indemnification obligations arising from acts or 
events that occurred while this Agreement was in effect; to give effect to the 
confidentiality and dispute resolution provisions; and to permit each Party to access 
the lands of the other to disconnect, remove, or salvage its facilities. 
ARTICLE 3 
SCOPE OF INTERCONNECTION SERVICE 
3.1 
Provision of Service. For purposes of this Agreement, Transmission Owner shall 
provide load interconnection service to Customer at the Point of Interconnection 
for the Term, up to the Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand, subject to this 
Agreement, the Tariff, and Applicable Laws and Regulations. 
3.2 
Load Limits. Customer shall ensure that the actual demand of the Load Facility 
does not exceed the Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand, the Maximum Annual

Energy, or the amount fully studied in the System Impact Study and Facilities 
Study, as measured at the Point of Interconnection.  
3.3 
Identification of Reliability Violation. If NYISO or Transmission Owner 
identifies a reliability violation associated with the Load Facility, at any time, 
Transmission Owner shall notify Customer of the amount of load that may be 
reliably served, and the Parties shall coordinate operational limitations or 
mitigation measures to minimize interruptions or reductions; Customer shall 
conform its load to such amount. 
3.4 
No Transmission Service or Other Services. This Agreement does not constitute 
a request for, or agreement to provide, transmission service under the Tariff, or the 
sale or purchase of energy, capacity, or ancillary services under the NYISO 
Services Tariff. Transmission Owner does not sell electric energy under this 
Agreement. Customer shall be solely responsible for arranging its energy supply 
and shall maintain a service agreement with a load serving entity for the Load 
Facility. All Delivery Service shall be provided pursuant to, and billed in 
accordance with, the applicable Tariff, and Customer shall select and qualify for 
the applicable service classification. Nothing in this Agreement obligates 
Transmission Owner to provide Delivery Service beyond the Tariff or to expand 
the transmission system beyond the facilities identified in the studies for the Load 
Facility. 
3.5 
Load Ramp Projection. Within ten (10) Business Days after the Effective Date, 
Customer shall provide monthly projections of energy and demand for the Term in 
the form of Exhibit A. On the fifth anniversary of the Effective Date and every fifth 
anniversary thereafter, Customer shall provide updated projections for the 
remainder of the Term (the most recent version, the “Load Ramp Projection”); 
provided that no update may change the monthly projections by more than [five 
percent (5%)] from the prior version (absent prior written authorization by 
Transmission Owner and NYISO), and in no event may the demand projection 
exceed the Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand or the annual energy projection 
exceed the Maximum Annual Energy.  
3.6 
Reduction of Interconnection Rights. If the Load Facility fails to meet the 
Minimum Committed Load for [three (3)] consecutive months or [three (3)] non-
consecutive months in any [six (6)]-month period after the Commercial Operation 
Date (a “Shortfall Event”), Transmission Owner may notify Customer that it 
intends to reduce the Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand if Customer does not 
consistently meet the Minimum Committed Load during the following sixty (60) 
Calendar Days. Any reduction shall be proportionate to the average load shortfall 
over the applicable period, and Exhibit A shall be amended accordingly, subject to 
any filing with or acceptance by FERC or the NYPSC required under Applicable 
Laws and Regulations. Any reduction of the Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand 
under this Article 3.6 shall not reduce Customer’s obligations under the Cost 
Recovery Agreement or the Security Amount under the Security Agreement. 
3.7 
Exceedance Events. Customer shall not permit the actual demand or energy 
consumption of the Load Facility to exceed the limits set forth in Article 3.2, and

Exceedance Events are not permitted under this Agreement. The parameters, 
thresholds, number and duration of occurrences, and other criteria that constitute 
an Exceedance Event shall be as set forth in Exhibits A and C. Upon the occurrence 
of an Exceedance Event, Transmission Owner may require Customer to reduce 
load, may interrupt Delivery Service in accordance with Article 7.4, and may 
require additional study at Customer’s cost to identify any further upgrades 
necessary to serve the Load Facility and additional security under the Security 
Agreement.  
ARTICLE 4 
CONDITIONS TO ENERGIZATION AND 
PERMISSION TO OPERATE 
4.1 
Conditions Precedent. Transmission Owner shall not energize the Load Facility 
or permit its parallel operation with the TO System until the conditions set forth in 
Exhibit F have been satisfied to Transmission Owner’s reasonable satisfaction. 
4.2 
Permission to Operate. Upon satisfaction of the conditions in Exhibit F, 
Transmission Owner shall issue PTO or identify in writing the deficiencies 
preventing issuance of PTO within a reasonable time after completion of required 
testing and receipt of all required documentation. 
4.3 
Parallel Operation. Upon issuance of PTO, Transmission Owner shall permit 
parallel operation of the Load Facility with the TO System subject to this 
Agreement, the Tariff, and Applicable Laws and Regulations. 
ARTICLE 5 
ENGINEERING, PROCUREMENT, AND 
CONSTRUCTION 
5.1 
Transmission Owner Construction. Transmission Owner shall use Reasonable 
Efforts to design, procure, construct, and install the TO Attachment Facilities and 
Network Upgrades described in Exhibit B by the milestone dates in Exhibit D. 
Transmission Owner will act in accordance with its safety practices, TO Standards, 
labor agreements, applicable agreements, and Applicable Laws and Regulations. If 
Transmission Owner reasonably expects not to meet a milestone, it shall promptly 
notify Customer (and NYISO, if required) and use Reasonable Efforts to meet the 
earliest practicable date thereafter. Milestones may otherwise be modified by 
mutual written agreement. 
5.2 
Customer Attachment Facilities. Customer shall, at its sole expense, design, 
procure, construct, own, install, operate, and maintain the Customer Attachment 
Facilities and the Load Facility described in Exhibit A in accordance with Good 
Utility Practice, TO Standards (including the specifications, technical manuals, and 
standards furnished by Transmission Owner), and Applicable Laws and 
Regulations. Customer shall submit design drawings and initial specifications for 
the Customer Attachment Facilities, including System Protection Facilities, for

Transmission Owner’s engineering review at least one hundred eighty (180) 
Calendar Days, and final specifications at least ninety (90) Calendar Days, before 
the In-Service Date. Transmission Owner shall comment within thirty (30) 
Calendar Days, and Customer shall make such changes as Transmission Owner 
reasonably requires for compatibility with its technical, operational, and safety 
requirements. At least ninety (90) Calendar Days before initial energization, 
Customer shall deliver as-built or redlined drawings and relay settings for the 
Customer Attachment Facilities, and within one hundred twenty (120) Calendar 
Days after the In-Service Date, Customer shall deliver final “as-built” drawings and 
relay settings. Customer shall use Reasonable Efforts to complete the Customer 
Attachment Facilities and its other activities by the Customer milestone dates in 
Exhibit D and acknowledges that Transmission Owner’s ability to meet its 
milestones may depend on Customer’s timely completion of such activities. 
5.3 
Affected Transmission Owner Construction. Facilities or Network Upgrades to 
be constructed by an Affected Transmission Owner shall be governed by a separate 
agreement between Customer and the applicable Affected Transmission Owner. 
Customer shall timely execute that agreement, provide all required payments, 
deposits, information, property rights, and financial security, and promptly notify 
Transmission Owner of any delay in, or change to, the scope or milestones under 
such agreement. Transmission Owner shall use Reasonable Efforts to coordinate its 
work with the Affected Transmission Owner but shall not be responsible for the 
Affected Transmission Owner’s acts, omissions, performance, or delays. Any 
Transmission Owner milestone dependent upon Affected Transmission Owner 
performance shall be equitably extended to reflect the resulting delay. Customer’s 
ability to receive service may be dependent on the completion of milestones under 
its agreements with the Affected Transmission Owner, and Transmission Owner 
shall not be required to energize the Load Facility, issue Permission to Operate, or 
authorize the applicable level of service until all required Affected Transmission 
Owner facilities have been completed and placed in service. 
5.4 
No Warranty. Transmission Owner’s review, approval, inspection, or acceptance 
of any design, specification, or facility shall not constitute an endorsement or 
warranty of its design, fitness, safety, durability, or reliability. TRANSMISSION 
OWNER DISCLAIMS ANY RESPONSIBILITY OR LIABILITY FOR THE

Force Majeure. “Force Majeure” means any event or circumstance beyond a 
Party’s reasonable control that prevents the Party from performing an obligation, is 
not the result of the negligence or intentional wrongdoing of such Party, and could 
not have been prevented or mitigated by the exercise of Good Utility Practice (in 
the case of Transmission Owner) or due diligence (in the case of Customer),

accident to machinery, epidemic or pandemic, cyber-attack (except to the extent 
caused by or resulting from Customer’s failure to comply with its obligations under 
this Agreement), sabotage, terrorism, war, civil disturbance, strikes and labor 
disturbances, acts or orders of any Governmental Authority, and curtailment or 
interruption directed by NYISO for reliability reasons. Force Majeure shall not 
include, with respect to Customer: (a) economic hardship, changes in market 
conditions, or the cost or unavailability of financing; (b) delays in Customer’s 
procurement of equipment or failure of Customer’s suppliers or contractors, unless

caused by an independent Force Majeure event; (c) labor disputes involving only 
Customer’s or its contractors’ workforce; (d) Customer’s failure to obtain required 
permits or approvals, unless it has diligently and timely pursued them; or (e) 
changes in the demand for, or the business case of, the Load Facility’s end use.

due or to timely post or maintain the Financial Security.

the obligation to pay money when due) to the extent prevented by Force Majeure,

(30) Calendar Days from receipt to cure; provided that (a) a Breach consisting of a 
failure to pay any amount when due or to provide, maintain, or replenish security 
shall be cured within five (5) Business Days after notice; (b) if a non-monetary
